whySwitch.title: Why growth teams don't stop at a store Agent and go straight to Cluega AI

items.title: Store operations are something Cluega AI already does — but it doesn't stop there
items.body: Once TikTok Shop／Amazon／Shopify are connected, listing optimisation, product and order data, and store diagnostics are carried out by Cluega's Agents and Skills all the same. The difference is the ceiling: however well you optimise listings and however clean your SEO, the limit is the traffic you already have; what really decides the growth curve is acquisition. Cluega puts store operations and paid growth in the same system — the time-saving work still gets done, and the revenue-scaling work gets done next.

items.title: Delegating spend needs a risk gate, not item-by-item approval
items.body: Store Agents demand item-by-item human approval for high-risk actions — especially anything touching money — and at scale that becomes approval fatigue. Cluega solves it with AAIGS: account maturity M0–M5 and the T0–T3 authorisation ladder determine how much budget the AI can commit on its own, with new accounts starting at low authorisation and earning more as data accumulates — an institutional gate between aggressive and out of control.

items.title: Revenue-share billing: one predictable line, all costs included
items.body: The pain of a credit system is "no idea how much this task will burn". Cluega's fully managed mode charges a single "ad spend × share" line (4%→2.5%→1.5%, decreasing with scale): tokens, images, short video and optimisation decisions along the way are all included, plus a $149／month managed base fee and fair-use guardrails, so small and large accounts alike can do the maths.

items.title: Private-domain attribution catches the sales the store can't see
items.body: A huge share of the world's sales aren't in the cart — they're in WhatsApp／LINE／Zalo DMs. StoreClaw's world ends at the store back office; Cluega pushes captured leads and closed sales from private-domain conversations back to the ad source, so the full chain from ad to sale finally adds up.

storeclaw.label: Choose StoreClaw
storeclaw.body: You're a small-to-mid seller or a solo store owner who only needs day-to-day store upkeep automated — inventory reminders, listing optimisation, social posts — with no plans to run ads at all and acquisition riding entirely on organic traffic.

cluega.label: Choose Cluega AI
cluega.body: You want one system that handles it end to end: store operations well looked after, while the AI buys media autonomously and auditably, creative capacity is wired into the budget, and private-domain sales attribution closes the loop — with fees tied directly to your ad performance instead of maintaining separate tools for store chores and growth.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you might want to know before you reach out to our team.

items.q: Can Cluega AI do the store-operations work that StoreClaw does?
items.a: It can. Once TikTok Shop／Amazon／Shopify are connected, operational work such as listing optimisation, product and order data sync, and store diagnostics is carried out by Cluega's Agents and Skills. The difference is architectural: Cluega puts store data, ad accounts and private-domain conversations on the same data foundation, so store work isn't an island — it's part of attribution and buying decisions.

items.q: What exactly is fully managed L4?
items.a: L4 denotes the autonomous AI buying tier: you hand the ad account to the AI and it decides bids, budgets, audiences and creative retirement on its own, with a tiered share of the ad spend it actually manages (4%→2.5%→1.5%). All token and creative-generation costs during that period are included, and you pay a single line.

There are three safeguards: the AAIGS authorisation ladder starts new accounts at low permissions; every decision carries an audit log you can trace back; and billing only counts spend attributed to Cluega's AD fingerprint, so campaigns you open manually don't count toward the share. The AI's spending authority is always tied to the account's data maturity.

items.q: Small team, no dedicated media buyer — is the barrier to entry high?
items.a: Not high. $12／week is enough to trial it, and from $99／month on Pro you can switch on fully managed (4% share, $149／month managed base fee); compared with hiring your own media buyer or a human agency's 10–15% service fee, that's an order of magnitude apart.
